text: The treatment changed-window read and the active-count read are published by the owner of the treatment record, on base /api/recovery/treatment/v1, with the right Treatment and offer R and a fake; rwb-source-data calls them from the snapshot(page) activity of its Stage2ProductWorkflow. Where RWB-P1-E2010-APP names the same two reads under the rwb-case contract, the ownership of the table treatment decides, and the consumer changes its fake only if the conflict is resolved the other way.
why: The legacy step called the treatment module in process, and the target cannot have two owners of the same read; leaving it open would block both the S2 slice and the DP04 build on Day 1.
read: Ownership Map v1 table treatment and S2 api rows; Template and Rules v1 R3 precedence, R4 and R5.5 DP-01, DP-11, DP-13; RWB-P1-E2010-APP section 12.2
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 2 entry check
impact: Medium: one read operation moves from the case base to the treatment base.

text: The two operations are GET /treatments with changedFrom, changedTo, page and size, and GET /treatments/active-count, both on /api/recovery/treatment/v1, ordered by updated_at and id, with page, size and total in the answer and a maximum size of 1000. A treatment counts as active when its outcome is empty and is_active is true; the state set is held as a parameter row of the parameters contract of rwb-case with its version. The lists are read through GET /api/recovery/case/v1/reference-data/{tableCode} on the rwb-case base, one hop and a 2 s timeout.
why: No source fixes an operation shape, a page size, an active rule or a consumer-facing reference-data read, and the DP04 build cannot be faked without them; the reference-data path is the one already assumed for the dictionary slice of this run.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-010 section 12; TSD S2 v2 T3.1 and T6.1; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-07 and DP-11; ASM-B-P1-02-E1064-101
confirm: Tech lead at the wave 2 entry check
impact: Low: a read shape and one parameter name, no business value.

text: The DP04 build reads the two operations under the service identity of rwb-source-data, which holds a right row of Treatment and offer R in the access data of rwb-access; the RBAC matrix of TSD S2 T6.1 lists people roles only and carries no row for a consuming service, so the service identity is granted the same read right as RW-CASEOWN and no more.
why: The consumer is a service, and the matrix of the module names no service identity; without a right row the DP04 build is refused with MSG-P4-002 and the stage 2 product can never be stamped.
read: TSD S2 v2 T6.1 and T6.2 (service identities for jobs and agents); Legacy RWB-E2-010 section 10; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 and R7.1 (rights are data)
confirm: Access and administration lead at the wave 2 entry check

text: The Work Package lists no build dependency, so the treatment table of schema rwb_treatment with DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-033 and the platform libraries on the service template (guard, reference-data client, Flyway baseline) are taken as present when this story starts, in the same lane as RWB-S2-E2004-APP. The feature switch rwb.treatment.stage2-read exists, defaults to off in the non-production environments, and the two operations answer 404 with MSG-P4-003 while it is off.
why: A story that must be Day 1 cannot wait for another build, and the reads have no meaning before the table exists; the switch keeps the unfinished wiring from exposing an unversioned answer.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.7 Day-1 rules and R7.1; RWB-S2-E2004-APP sections 3 and 13; Work Package B2-S2-018 line for RWB-S2-E2010-APP
confirm: Tech lead at the wave 2 entry check
impact: Low: delivery sequencing and one flag, no behaviour change.
